readout_other: volumetric multispectral optoacoustic tomography (HbO, HbR, HbT)
direction_notes: hTUS evoked brain-wide hemodynamic responses (HbO, HbR, HbT) that extended beyond the focus; lower pressure produced a weaker or slower response. Neuronal excitation or inhibition was not measured.

timing.protocol_description: During the 15.2 s of the TUS stimulation, 100 ms US pulses at 3 MHz are repeated at 4 Hz (40% duty cycle); pulse duration was also reduced to 50 ms. Five stimulations spaced by 40 s were delivered.

source_quotes.n_subjects: Pelleted food (3437PXL15, CARGILL) and water were provided ad-libitum. A total of 3 female C57BL/6J mice were employed for this study.
source_quotes.exposures[0].fundamental_frequency_khz: The light is distributed over a large (\~1 cm<sup>2</sup>) area on the mouse head to yield a maximum fluence of 10 ${ \mathrm { m J / c m } } ^ { 2 } ,$ well below the maximum permissible exposure limit in the NIR spectrum (>20 mJ/cm<sup>2</sup>) [37]. The laser is tuned to five different wavelengths (730, 755, 780, 800, and 850 nm) on a per pulse basis at a pulse repetition rate of 100 Hz (Fig. 1B). During the 15.2 s of the TUS stimulation, the 100 ms duration US pulses at 3 MHz carrier frequency are repeated at 4 Hz (40 % duty cycle).

Transcranial pressure is measured using a mouse skull, as described elsewhere [23]. A peak pressure of 1.2 MPa $( \mathrm { I } _ { \mathrm { S P P A } } = 4 8 \mathrm { \ W / c m ^ { 2 } } )$ and $0 . 9 \ \mathrm { M P a } \ ( \mathrm { I } _ { \mathrm { S P P A } } = 2 7 \ \mathrm { W } / \mathrm { c m } ^ { 2 } )$ was estimated in the mouse brain using the previously measured 6 dB skull insertion loss at 3 MHz [23]. Thus, the highest pressure yields mechanical index of 0.7.

source_quotes.exposures[0].timing.pulse_duration_ms: In addition, we varied the peak pressure between 1.2 and 0.9 MPa and the US pulse duration between 100 and 50 ms.
source_quotes.exposures[0].timing.pulse_repetition_fre: It is important to clarify how our approach compares to previous studies where concerns have been raised about potential auditory confounds in TUS experiments [47,48] First, we used longer sonication durations (50–100 ms per pulse), which differ significantly from the 1.5 kHz envelope used in Ref. [47]. As a result, our pulse repetition frequency (4–8 Hz) lies outside the mouse hearing range [49]. Second, the compact ultrasound focus size in our system is specifically tailored for precise targeting in the mouse brain.

flags.reason: Peak pressures 1.2 and 0.9 MPa (Isppa 48 and 27 W/cm2) are derated from free-field using a 6 dB skull insertion loss; the paper's 'peak pressure' is not stated as free-field separately.
Ispta (19 and 11 W/cm2) is given in a figure legend without a domain.
Methods give 4 Hz for 100 ms pulses; the discussion gives 4-8 Hz, so 8 Hz presumably applies to 50 ms pulses at the same duty cycle (not stated directly).
Abstract says 15 s; methods say 15.2 s.
No auditory control during the experiment; the discussion argues from prior work and from absence of auditory cortex hemodynamic signal, and says controls are future work.
Custom 512-element array from Imasonic; driven by Falkenstein Mikrosysteme electronics.
